theses.title: Real assets hedge persistent inflation and supply uncertainty.
theses.worldView: Fiscal demand, supply constraints, or geopolitical disruption will keep inflation and commodity volatility above a benign baseline often enough for real assets to diversify financial assets, even if real growth moderates. The claim is falsified by durable disinflation, stable supply and falling energy and gold prices.
theses.portfolioExpression: XLE.US and GLD.US are modest, unlevered real-asset exposures rather than return guarantees; their sizing recognizes that both can fall together in a growth shock and that the snapshot does not establish either as cheap on a valuation multiple.

theses.title: Growth and rates stay uncertain, so liquidity has option value.
theses.worldView: Policy rates, inflation expectations and credit conditions will remain uncertain rather than following a frictionless disinflation path, with a moderate slowdown more likely than a depression; short-duration liquidity should therefore retain resilience and intermediate bonds have upside if yields fall. The claim is falsified if a sustained inflation shock drives both bonds and cash-like assets lower in real terms or if an unexpectedly powerful boom makes them a large opportunity cost.
theses.portfolioExpression: AGG.US and SHY.US provide different duration exposures, and 10% cash is intentionally uninvested and earns 0% but limits portfolio sensitivity and preserves resilience; that drag resolves the tension between participation and drawdown control.

pick.thesis: This is a fixed buy-and-hold barbell: value and non-US breadth are the return engine, healthcare, staples and industrial exposure supply essential-demand balance, a modest energy and gold sleeve covers real-asset uncertainty, and bonds plus cash address rate and recession risk. The central tension is that a growth slowdown can hurt international and industrial equities while inflation can hurt bonds, so neither scenario is allowed to dominate the allocation. The 10% cash is deliberate dry powder and drawdown control rather than an accidental remainder, although it earns 0% and will not be reallocated.

forecasts.reason: A 9% total return is plausible if equity leadership broadens toward value and non-US markets, healthcare and staples remain resilient, industrial investment avoids a deep recession, and rates stabilize or ease enough for AGG.US to recover part of its recent weakness. The bond, cash and gold sleeves will create a drag in a strong risk-on market, but they should reduce the cost of an inflationary or recessionary surprise; the outcome remains uncertain and could be materially higher or lower.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: The frozen packet ends on 2026-09-28 and provides adjusted daily prices, three-month and twelve-month returns, 52-week ranges, asset classes and observation counts, but it does not provide current valuation multiples, earnings, balance sheets, dividend yields, duration, constituent weights, fees or future macro data. I therefore use the quoted price and return or range evidence plus durable knowledge of each ETF's broad exposure, and I treat every catalyst, relative-value judgment and macro path as an assumption rather than a verified fact. I cannot know events after the cutoff or whether any thesis will hold, so the forecast and drawdown estimate are uncertain.

strategies.riskRationale: This allocation fits medium risk over 12 months because it accepts meaningful equity exposure while spreading it across US value, a small broad-market core, developed and emerging markets, defensive and cyclical sectors, rather than depending on one company or speculative asset. It adds 14% in bond ETFs, 8% in gold-linked exposure, and 10% in cash, so upside is sacrificed for resilience and cash earns 0%. I estimate a target-period maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of 18%, with a materially larger loss possible in a correlated global shock.

pick.risks: An AI-capex slowdown, recession, restrictive real rates or a broad risk-off episode could hit nearly every position at once; ADBE.US, INTU.US, ZS.US, AMAT.US and KLAC.US make up 54% and may correlate through technology multiples, GEV.US and FCX.US add cyclical industrial and commodity sensitivity, crypto can suffer very large independent collapses, and single-name execution, regulation, geopolitics, supply shocks and the absence of rebalancing remain material risks.

theses.title: AI diffusion sustains physical capex
theses.worldView: Over the next 12 months, AI adoption broadens into enterprise and industrial workloads, keeping semiconductor manufacturing investment, process-control demand and electricity infrastructure spending resilient; this thesis is falsified by a sustained global capex recession, a rapid AI cost collapse that halts new capacity, or a sharp demand slowdown.
theses.portfolioExpression: The portfolio uses AMAT.US and KLAC.US as semiconductor-equipment picks and shovels and GEV.US as power-generation and electrification exposure, accepting that these are correlated cyclical bets rather than buying only the most expensive AI leaders.

theses.title: AI augments installed software workflows
theses.worldView: Businesses will generally add AI to trusted creative, financial-administration and cybersecurity workflows faster than they replace the underlying systems during the forecast year, so software spending survives a valuation reset; this thesis is falsified by widespread substitution, budget cuts or persistent price compression.
theses.portfolioExpression: ADBE.US, INTU.US and ZS.US express this as contrarian exposure to established workflow and security platforms whose snapshot prices are materially below their 52-week highs, with the price dislocations treated as hypotheses rather than proof of cheapness.

theses.title: Strategic resources stay scarce
theses.worldView: Electrification, grid build-out, supply-chain redundancy and geopolitical fragmentation keep demand for copper and power equipment above a benign oversupply baseline; this thesis is falsified by a global industrial recession, a large supply response or a durable fall in energy and materials intensity.
theses.portfolioExpression: FCX.US and the physical-capex sleeve express this thesis through copper and power bottlenecks, adding a non-software source of upside while preserving cyclical exposure.

theses.title: Digital monetary and network assets regain liquidity
theses.worldView: Over the next year, an improvement or stabilization in global liquidity and continued use of permissionless settlement and smart-contract networks can lift scarce digital assets after their recent underperformance; this thesis is falsified by prolonged restrictive liquidity, hostile regulation, security failures or adoption that fails to translate into token demand.
theses.portfolioExpression: BTC-USD.CC, ETH-USD.CC and SOL-USD.CC are held as unlevered spot optionality only, with no staking or lending, and their sizes recognize that network adoption, token economics and market structure remain uncertain.

pick.thesis: Together these theses form a high-beta barbell with 54% in software and semiconductor exposure, 18% in power and copper, 19% in spot digital assets and 9% in cash; the growth and capex theses can benefit from strong investment, while the resource and digital sleeves offer different inflation and liquidity outcomes. The 9% cash is an explicit expression of the view that a high-dispersion regime can produce a better entry point or temporary thesis failure, and it earns 0% rather than being a leftover allocation.

forecasts.reason: A 24% total return is plausible if AI-related capex remains resilient, software is shown to be augmented rather than displaced, power and copper stay relatively tight and global liquidity or network adoption supports a crypto recovery; those conditions could let the beaten-down software and semiconductor positions plus digital assets outperform, although a recession or rates shock could instead produce a large negative result.

positions.name: Adobe

positions.catalyst: An observable catalyst would be evidence that AI features are monetized inside the installed workflow and that recurring demand stabilizes, allowing a valuation re-rating over the year.
positions.invalidation: The application fails if customers substitute away from core creative or document workflows, AI tools commoditize the product, software budgets contract or the stock remains cheap because cash flows deteriorate; the 13% weight is large enough to matter for a high-risk rebound but below a single-theme majority.

positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be a broad software-spending recovery plus user retention and successful AI-assisted workflow monetization, which could narrow the reset.
positions.invalidation: The thesis is wrong if AI-native or low-cost alternatives displace the installed products, weak small-business activity reduces demand or the price decline reflects permanent economic impairment; the 10% weight acknowledges more uncertainty than ADBE.US while retaining asymmetric upside.

positions.invalidation: The application is invalidated by a security failure, commoditization, customer budget cuts or competition that prevents pricing power; the 8% size limits damage from a single security name while retaining high-beta upside.

positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be utility, industrial and data-center power orders converting into sustained backlog and cash generation, alongside a broader market preference for physical capex.
positions.invalidation: It is wrong if electricity demand disappoints, projects are delayed by rates or permitting, supply catches up or the prior run leaves no margin of safety; the 8% weight keeps this high-volatility industrial bet from dominating the book.

positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be sustained copper demand with constrained mine supply or a new investment cycle in grids and electrification, lifting realized prices and the sector multiple.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails with a global manufacturing recession, substitution or oversupply, falling copper prices, labor or permitting disruption or mine-specific cost problems; the 10% weight is enough to diversify away from software but recognizes high commodity beta.

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.thesis: BTC-USD.CC is unlevered spot exposure to the Bitcoin network and its scarce digital-monetary asset. It applies the digital-liquidity-optionality thesis because the snapshot price is $83,856.60, down 5.0% over 12 months and 6.3% below the $89,503.88 52-week high, so the allocation is a contrarian liquidity and adoption option rather than a claim of intrinsic cash-flow value; the mechanism depends on fixed-supply demand, custody access and continued market acceptance.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be improving global liquidity and sustained institutional, corporate or individual demand for non-sovereign digital scarcity, producing a new risk-appetite cycle.
positions.invalidation: It is invalidated by prolonged restrictive liquidity, regulation that impairs access, a protocol or custody failure, loss of trust or a major risk-off liquidation; the 9% weight is large enough for upside but limits portfolio dependence on an asset with no operating cash flow.

positions.name: Ether
positions.thesis: ETH-USD.CC is spot ether, the native asset of a programmable smart-contract network. It applies the digital-liquidity-optionality thesis because $2,713.20 is 7.6% below its 12-month starting level and 10.2% below the $3,022.21 52-week high, giving a smaller reset than the software names; the mechanism is that network usage and settlement demand can create token demand, but supply dynamics, fees, competition and protocol changes are assumptions.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be renewed on-chain activity and liquidity that makes programmable settlement and applications economically important, followed by a broader crypto re-rating.
positions.invalidation: It is wrong if usage migrates to competing chains or centralized systems, token economics dilute demand, security or regulation damages access or restrictive liquidity persists; the 6% weight reflects meaningful upside with less confidence than BTC-USD.CC, and no staking yield is assumed.

positions.name: Solana
positions.thesis: SOL-USD.CC is spot exposure to Solana's smart-contract network token. It applies the digital-liquidity-optionality thesis at $120.68, down 4.0% over 12 months and 6.7% below the $129.38 52-week high after a 63.7% three-month rally; the value case is high-throughput network adoption and liquidity optionality rather than a verified cash-flow valuation, and it depends on reliability, developer and user demand and token economics.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be sustained transaction and application adoption with improving market liquidity, allowing the network to capture more of the next crypto cycle.
positions.invalidation: A prolonged outage or security problem, weak usage, intense competition, regulatory restrictions, inflationary token pressure or crypto-wide deleveraging would invalidate it; the 4% weight is a deliberately small high-risk option because downside can be extreme.

theses.title: Inflation moderates without a synchronized boom.
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months, inflation and policy rates stop rising while real activity remains positive but uneven; the claim is falsified by a renewed inflation shock that forces materially higher rates or by a deep recession with broad credit stress.
theses.portfolioExpression: The portfolio expresses this view with 30% in SHY.US and AGG.US, 41% in diversified value, dividend, defensive, and developed-market equities, and 25% in cash, so it can benefit from normalized bonds and resilient earnings without depending on a strong boom.

theses.title: Cash-flow breadth can catch up with concentrated growth leadership.
theses.worldView: Over the horizon, mature cash-flow and dividend exposures, defensive sectors, or developed markets outside the United States will have at least one period of relative leadership; this is falsified if concentrated growth leadership persists and these exposures lag without a compensating risk reduction.
theses.portfolioExpression: The snapshot shows SPY.US and QQQ.US near their 52-week highs, although it does not prove overvaluation, so VTV.US, SCHD.US, XLP.US, XLV.US, BRK-B.US, and EFA.US provide breadth rather than a single growth bet.

theses.title: Monetary and geopolitical shocks remain possible.
theses.worldView: During the 24-month period, inflation surprises, fiscal or currency stress, and geopolitical supply disruptions remain plausible enough to justify insurance; this is falsified for the portfolio if stable disinflation and high real rates make gold and liquidity consistently costly without any risk-off episode.
theses.portfolioExpression: The 25% cash allocation and 4% GLD.US allocation are explicit capital-preservation and shock-insurance positions, while the bond sleeve avoids long-duration concentration and the portfolio uses no crypto or leverage; cash is held as ballast for the fixed horizon, not as a promise to trade.

pick.thesis: This is a fixed, long-only defensive barbell with 25% cash, 30% bond ETFs, 41% diversified equity exposures, and 4% gold. The portfolio treats value as durable cash-flow breadth and reduced drawdown sensitivity at the snapshot prices, not as a claim of verified low valuation multiples; the cash and bonds resolve the tension between wanting a recovery in risk assets and protecting a low-risk two-year objective. No crypto is included because its spot volatility and lack of contractual cash flow are not needed to express these theses at low risk.

forecasts.reason: An 8% total return is plausible if inflation cools without a deep recession, bond prices stop being pressured by rising yields, and value, dividend, defensive, and non-U.S. equities deliver moderate positive adjusted returns; the 25% cash allocation caps upside, while a renewed inflation shock or synchronized equity-and-bond selloff could make the outcome much lower.

positions.name: Short-Maturity U.S. Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: SHY.US is short-maturity U.S. Treasury exposure, so it applies the disinflation thesis through relatively low interest-rate sensitivity and the shock-insurance thesis through liquid sovereign exposure. The known snapshot price is $81.11 on 2026-09-28, with a $79.97-$81.84 52-week range and a 1.49% twelve-month adjusted return; at that price I value its relative stability role rather than claim it is cheap or that its current yield is known. Its durable mechanism is short maturity and contractual bond cash flows, and the 15% weight belongs here because low risk needs a meaningful ballast but not a full cash replacement.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be stable or falling short-term rates, a flight to quality, or the ordinary reinvestment of maturing short bonds, although I cannot verify the current yield or forward return.
positions.invalidation: This application is wrong if inflation forces a sustained rise in short rates, sovereign liquidity is impaired, or nominal stability masks a large loss of purchasing power; its 15% size limits but does not eliminate those risks.

positions.name: Broad U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF
positions.thesis: AGG.US is a broad U.S. investment-grade bond-market ETF spanning government and credit exposure, so it applies the disinflation thesis by offering duration and income diversification and the insurance thesis through a non-equity asset. Its known adjusted close is $94.65, exactly the supplied 52-week low, after a -1.50% twelve-month return; that rate-driven weakness creates a reason to own recovery potential at this price, but it is not proof of a cheap yield or intrinsic value because those data are not supplied. theses.title: Productivity capital broadens beyond the leaders.
theses.worldView: Over the 24-month period, enterprise digitization, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and AI-assisted workflows will continue to attract enough spending for productivity gains to broaden beyond a few headline companies; the claim is falsified by broad capital-expenditure digestion, weak adoption, or a persistent technology profit de-rating.
theses.portfolioExpression: I express this with 5% MSFT.US and 4% ADBE.US plus diluted technology exposure in VTI.US, while keeping the combined direct exposure small enough that an AI boom is not required.

theses.title: Physical investment and real assets retain scarcity value.
theses.worldView: Over the 24-month period, grid, infrastructure, industrial replacement, and energy needs will remain large enough that nominal growth and supply constraints support selected real-asset cash flows; the claim is falsified by a deep global recession, durable commodity oversupply, or a sharp collapse in physical investment.
theses.portfolioExpression: I express this with 7% XLI.US and 6% XLE.US, supported by the industrial and energy exposure already embedded in VTI.US and EFA.US, rather than through a concentrated commodity bet.

theses.title: Valuation dispersion rewards broad value and quality.
theses.worldView: Over the 24-month period, uneven returns and high concentration leave room for diversified value, quality, and non-U.S. equities to mean-revert relative to crowded or higher-duration growth; the claim is falsified if mega-cap growth keeps dominating and value's structural headwinds persist.
theses.portfolioExpression: I express this with 18% VTI.US, 14% VTV.US, 8% EFA.US, and 9% BRK-B.US, with a 10% XLV.US sleeve to add resilient quality; these positions seek breadth and mean reversion rather than a single cheap stock.

theses.title: Uncertainty makes liquidity and monetary hedges valuable.
theses.worldView: Over the 24-month period, recession, inflation, interest-rate, fiscal, or geopolitical shocks remain plausible enough that liquid reserves and gold can improve portfolio resilience even if they lag in a smooth expansion; the claim is falsified by stable disinflation and uninterrupted risk appetite that make these hedges persistently costly.
theses.portfolioExpression: I express this with 6% GLD.US, 5% SHY.US, and 8% cash; the reserve is intentional dry powder and volatility control, not an unallocated remainder.

pick.thesis: The portfolio is a fixed, no-rebalancing core of value and quality equities, with smaller digital-productivity and physical-investment sleeves and explicit shock insurance. The central tension is that upside requires participation in risk assets while the liquidity thesis says the supplied market levels may be fragile; the 8% cash, 5% SHY.US, and 6% GLD.US resolve that tension by accepting return drag rather than trying to time a regime change.

forecasts.reason: A 24-month total return of 0.15 is plausible if the world avoids a deep recession, digital and physical investment broaden into durable cash flows, value and non-U.S. equities close part of their relative gap, and gold or short Treasuries provide some protection without a prolonged rates shock. The estimate is deliberately below a high-growth outcome because 8% cash earns 0%, several equity sleeves begin near supplied highs, and a hard landing or persistent inflation could make the realized return negative.

strategies.riskRationale: This is a medium-risk allocation for 24 months because 81% is diversified but correlated equity exposure, while 6% gold, 5% short Treasuries, and 8% cash provide partial shock resistance. It accepts meaningful drawdowns and some near-high entry prices in exchange for upside from value dispersion, digital productivity, and physical investment, but it avoids leverage, crypto, and dependence on one speculative outcome. The estimated 29% maximum peak-to-trough loss is material, yet lower than an all-equity concentration would plausibly be, and the two-year horizon gives the cyclical sleeves some time to mean-revert.

CAT.US and FCX.US add cyclicality rather than reliable diversification, and BTC-USD.CC can lose most of its value in a liquidity or regulatory shock; recession, inflation, rates, supply-chain disruption, geopolitical conflict, execution failures, dilution and unknown liabilities could make the 0.58 drawdown estimate too low. The 5% cash allocation earns 0% and cannot be redeployed under the fixed-hold rule, so it is only a small buffer.

theses.title: AI capital spending broadens beyond the headline designers.
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months, spending on compute, advanced wafers, process control and cloud capacity remains above a normal replacement cycle and broadens beyond a few AI designers; the claim is falsified by a broad multi-quarter capital-spending cut, falling utilization or evidence that AI workloads do not support durable demand.
theses.portfolioExpression: The portfolio expresses this with a 37% core in AMAT.US, LRCX.US, KLAC.US and TSM.US, plus ORCL.US as a smaller cloud-and-database bridge, accepting cyclical and geopolitical risk for upside if the investment cycle broadens.

theses.title: AI productivity causes a software reset before monetization.
theses.worldView: Generative AI changes the economics of enterprise and creative software over 24 months, causing pricing and valuation pressure before successful incumbents turn distribution, workflow integration and trusted data into paid productivity; the claim is falsified if substitution overwhelms retention or if sector-wide AI monetization never appears.
theses.portfolioExpression: The book allocates 32% to ADBE.US, INTU.US and ORCL.US, with the largest weights in snapshot drawdowns, so it buys a potential re-rating after disruption has been priced rather than assuming software is risk-free.

theses.title: Physical investment meets constrained resources.
theses.worldView: Fiscal infrastructure, electrification, defense, reshoring and energy-transition investment keep demand for selected machinery and copper ahead of flexible supply over two years; the claim is falsified by a global recession, collapsing commodity prices or enough new supply to remove scarcity premiums.
theses.portfolioExpression: CAT.US and FCX.US receive 16% as high-beta physical-economy exposures, giving the book a partial non-software counterweight but not a dependable recession hedge.

theses.title: Monetary fragmentation supports scarce digital settlement.
theses.worldView: Fiscal stress, geopolitical fragmentation and increasing digital-asset adoption preserve demand for a scarce permissionless monetary and settlement network over 24 months, while liquidity remains cyclical; the claim is falsified by sustained real-rate pressure, regulatory exclusion, security failure or falling usage and liquidity.
theses.portfolioExpression: The 10% spot BTC-USD.CC position provides convex upside to that regime without leverage, and its size acknowledges that the thesis can fail catastrophically.

theses.title: Valuation dispersion rewards patience.
theses.worldView: Market leadership can remain narrow and correlations can rise during shocks while contrarian assets need time to repair, so a small cash allocation is rational even at zero return; the claim is falsified if risk assets compound smoothly and the cash drag dominates throughout the hold.
theses.portfolioExpression: Five percent stays in cash at the benchmark's zero return as deliberate underexposure to correlated risk and a modest drawdown buffer, not as an unallocated remainder or a plan to trade later.

pick.thesis: The book combines a bullish but falsifiable AI-capex view with a contrarian software reset, a physical-scarcity sleeve and a monetary-fragmentation option. The tensions are resolved by capping near-high exposures and retaining 5% cash, but the resulting correlations remain high and diversification may fail in a broad risk-off event.

forecasts.reason: A 34% total return is plausible only if AI infrastructure spending remains durable, the battered software names convert AI into retention or paid productivity, industrial and copper demand stays tight and Bitcoin benefits from renewed liquidity or monetary-fragmentation demand. Because these drivers can fail together, this is an uncertain point estimate for an un-rebalanced book rather than a confidence claim.

theses.portfolioExpression: Keep 5% in cash, which earns 0% and is an intentional, small buffer for a fixed, no-rebalancing portfolio. It is not deployable dry powder under these rules and accepts a modest return drag.

pick.thesis: This is a concentrated contrarian recovery book, not a claim that recent highs represent fair value. Half the portfolio assumes enterprise software can adapt to AI, 30% assumes consumer and housing demand stabilize, and 15% expresses comparatively resilient animal-health spending. Falling prices may reflect lasting impairment rather than opportunity, and the small cash allocation only modestly cushions that risk.

forecasts.reason: A +16% total return is plausible if enterprise software spending persists, AI complements incumbent workflows, household and housing demand stabilize, and animal-health demand remains comparatively resilient. Several deeply depressed holdings would need to recover at least part of their losses; failed assumptions or further valuation compression could instead make the portfolio materially negative.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.thesis: Oracle provides enterprise database and cloud infrastructure services, so it applies the thesis that business data workloads and incumbent systems persist in an AI economy. At the 2026-09-28 packet close of $132.60, its 12-month return was -54.0%, far below its $310.01 52-week high; that reset could offer conditional value if mission-critical workloads and switching costs endure. The packet has no earnings or valuation data to confirm cheapness. A 20% weight makes the contrarian view matter while limiting exposure to cloud-capex and competition risk.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be evidence that cloud and data workloads or enterprise renewals are growing enough to support returns on infrastructure spending; I cannot verify current backlog or guidance.
positions.invalidation: The application fails if enterprise spending slows, AI workloads do not earn adequate returns, or customers migrate away from Oracle's systems enough to erode renewals and margins. The low price could reflect lasting business damage.

positions.name: Adobe
positions.thesis: Adobe sells tools for creative and document workflows, applying the thesis that AI can complement rather than replace established software. At the packet close of $231.01, its 12-month return was -34.8% and it was well below its $360.37 52-week high. Familiar workflows and an established creative ecosystem could support value at this reset price if customers continue paying for them, but no current renewal, adoption or multiple data is supplied. The 18% weight is substantial but stops short of treating that outcome as certain.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be greater paid use of AI-assisted creative tools or stabilizing subscriptions as users incorporate AI into existing workflows; no current adoption metric or product event is assumed.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if AI alternatives commoditize creative work, customers migrate to substitutes or paid subscription demand weakens persistently. A further price decline would not, by itself, prove mispricing.

positions.name: Intuit
positions.thesis: Intuit provides tax-preparation and small-business accounting software, applying the thesis that recurring compliance and financial workflows remain valuable as AI develops. Its packet close was $269.40, a -60.7% 12-month return, near its $253.95 low and far below its $690.50 52-week high. Tax obligations, records and familiar workflows could support retention and productivity gains, making the price reset potentially attractive if those mechanisms persist; the packet cannot establish intrinsic value. The 12% weight reflects the large possible rebound but also the severe disruption risk.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be durable customer retention through tax and accounting cycles and useful adoption of AI-enabled workflows; the packet supplies no current renewal metrics or results.
positions.invalidation: The application fails if AI or platform competitors automate these tasks without Intuit retaining customer value, if customers switch in significant numbers, or if small-business demand weakens enough to impair renewals.

positions.name: Nike
positions.thesis: Nike is a global athletic-footwear and apparel business, applying the thesis that household discretionary demand avoids a deep downturn. At the packet close of $36.39, its 12-month return was -45.7%; it was only slightly above its $35.51 52-week low and well below its $72.19 high. A scaled brand and distribution network could benefit if consumer demand normalizes, but that general mechanism does not verify current brand strength or execution. The 15% weight gives the contrarian recovery case meaningful exposure while recognizing substantial company-specific risk.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be stabilizing discretionary spending and consumers responding to future product assortments without persistent discounting; this is a prospective mechanism, not a claim about current news.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if household spending stays weak or Nike's brand relevance and demand remain impaired, showing that the price decline reflects more than a cyclical trough.

positions.name: Home Depot
positions.thesis: Home Depot is a home-improvement retailer exposed to maintenance, remodeling and housing turnover. Its packet close of $289.89 equaled its 52-week low, and its 12-month return was -26.8%; the $398.80 high shows the scale of the reset. A large installed housing stock and deferred repair needs could support value if turnover and financing conditions stop worsening, but the packet does not establish valuation or current demand. A 15% weight adds cyclical upside while limiting exposure that could correlate with Nike in a downturn.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be stabilization in housing turnover and financing conditions that allows postponed repair and remodeling work to resume; no current rates or housing figures are verified.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if housing turnover, credit conditions or household budgets deteriorate further, or if deferred projects do not return. Trading at the packet's 52-week low does not make the stock intrinsically cheap.

positions.name: Zoetis
positions.thesis: Zoetis develops animal-health medicines and vaccines, applying the thesis that veterinary treatment and preventive-care needs are relatively recurring. At the packet close of $71.43, its 12-month return was -48.4%, near its $70.27 low and far below its $144.75 high. Those recurring needs could make the reset valuable if demand and the company's position hold, but the packet cannot verify current earnings or product prospects. The 15% weight supplies a distinct demand exposure while recognizing single-company and product risks.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would resilient veterinary-care demand and successful adoption of animal-health products; no specific pipeline result or product launch is assumed.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if animal-health demand proves more cyclical than assumed or competition, regulation or product setbacks materially weaken volumes or pricing.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: The frozen packet supplies adjusted closes, returns and 52-week ranges, but not current earnings, valuation multiples, balance sheets, interest rates, adoption metrics or the causes of individual price declines. Business descriptions and durable mechanisms reflect general knowledge, not verified 2026 company updates; a large fall from a high is not proof of intrinsic value.

strategies.riskRationale: This high-risk book puts 95% in six individual equities, including a 50% concentration in software and several holdings near their 52-week lows. It relies on uncertain mean reversion and accepts an estimated 45% peak-to-trough drawdown, with losses beyond that possible; the 5% cash allocation is only a small buffer.

pick.risks: An inflation shock could push yields up while weighing on VTV.US and PEP.US, while a recession could hurt equity demand and widen credit spreads in AGG.US; bonds and equities are not reliable diversifiers in every scenario. PEP.US may overlap with VTV.US, and the portfolio is predominantly U.S. and USD exposure. I estimate a 12% peak-to-trough decline in a plausible adverse path, not a maximum-loss guarantee; correlated rate and equity losses could exceed it.

theses.title: Rates remain two-sided
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months, I expect U.S. growth to cool without a deep deflationary recession, while nominal rates have at least one meaningful repricing rather than falling smoothly. Sustained deflation with a steady bond rally would falsify this base case.
theses.portfolioExpression: I hold 40% SHY.US and 15% AGG.US, with 25% cash, and avoid a large long-duration position. The supplied 12-month returns of +1.5% for SHY.US and -1.5% for AGG.US are consistent with recent rate uncertainty, though they do not prove what rates will do next. Cash earns 0% under the rules and is a deliberate buffer, not a return source.

theses.title: Everyday cash flows endure
theses.worldView: In a modest-growth, non-recessionary base case, essential household demand and diversified value-oriented businesses can sustain cash flows without relying on a narrow high-growth valuation boom. Broad profit and distribution weakness, or a persistent collapse in relative returns for value and staples, would falsify this view.
theses.portfolioExpression: I limit equities to 20%: 15% VTV.US provides a broad value-style basket and 5% PEP.US expresses recurring household essentials demand. This is a limited participation in the cash-flow thesis, not a claim that either holding is demonstrably cheap from the supplied data.

pick.thesis: The book assumes neither a deep recession nor a guaranteed bond rally. I resolve the tension by keeping 80% outside equities, favoring short Treasuries over long-duration debt, and capping the cash-flow equity sleeve at 20%. I accept likely underperformance versus SPY.US in a strong bull market in exchange for a more defensive mix.

forecasts.reason: A 5% nominal total return over 24 months is a cautious base case if the U.S. avoids a deep recession, bond interest and reinvestment roughly offset price volatility, and VTV.US and PEP.US cash flows hold up without a major valuation re-rating. The 25% cash sleeve earns 0%, and rising rates or an equity slump could make the realized return negative.

positions.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: SHY.US provides exposure to short-maturity U.S. Treasury bonds. At the frozen 2026-09-28 close of $81.11, its reported 12-month return was +1.5% and its 52-week range was $79.97-$81.84; shorter-maturity bonds generally have less price sensitivity to a given yield move than longer-duration bonds. That makes it a value-for-stability anchor at this price, not a claim that it is mispriced or has an attractive yield. The 40% weight reflects the priority on nominal stability.
positions.catalyst: Treasury interest distributions and reinvestment as short-dated bonds mature could contribute to total return, while falling short rates could provide a modest price tailwind; I assume no specific current yield.
positions.invalidation: A sharp inflation-driven rise in short yields could cause a nominal loss, and inflation could erode its real value. SHY.US can fall and is not a cash substitute.

positions.name: iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF
positions.thesis: AGG.US provides broad U.S. investment-grade bond exposure, including government, agency, mortgage-backed, and corporate debt. Its frozen close was $94.65, at the reported 52-week low, after a reported 12-month return of -1.5%; the weaker recent price and diversified bond exposure create a conditional value case if yields stabilize or fall. This does not establish an attractive current yield or fair value, and its greater rate and credit sensitivity than SHY.US is why the position is limited to 15%.
positions.catalyst: Interest distributions and reinvestment, together with cooling inflation and stable credit spreads, could support total return; a recession-driven fall in government yields could also partly offset equity weakness.
positions.invalidation: Persistent inflation or rising yields, widening corporate spreads, or mortgage-credit stress could push bond prices down alongside equities and show that the 52-week low was not a bargain.

positions.name: Vanguard Value ETF
positions.thesis: VTV.US provides a diversified U.S. value-style equity basket, applying the thesis through broad exposure rather than a bet on one company. At the supplied $218.38 close it had gained 21.0% over 12 months and was about 3.6% below its 52-week high, so the snapshot does not demonstrate that it is cheap. It belongs at 15% because the portfolio favors diversified value-oriented exposure over concentrated speculative risk, while the modest weight recognizes that this is not a proven margin-of-safety opportunity.
positions.catalyst: If the economy avoids recession, underlying company cash flows and distributions could support returns, and broader market leadership shifting toward value could add relative performance without requiring a major valuation expansion.
positions.invalidation: A deep recession and broad earnings or distribution cuts could drive losses, while sustained growth-led market leadership could make VTV.US lag. The supplied data contain no valuation ratios to rule out overvaluation.

positions.name: PepsiCo, Inc.
positions.thesis: PepsiCo sells packaged foods and beverages, so it expresses the view that household repeat-purchase demand can persist through slower growth. At the supplied $128.50 close it was near its $128.15 52-week low and about 22% below its $165.45 high; its reported 12-month return was -4.4%. This price weakness offers a conditional relative-value case if essential-demand cash flows hold up, but a past high is not fair value. The 5% weight limits single-company, input-cost, and consumer-preference risk.
positions.catalyst: If demand remains resilient and any input-cost or price-volume pressure eases, improved confidence in future cash flows could support a recovery without requiring extraordinary growth.
positions.invalidation: Sustained volume losses, consumers shifting to alternatives, costs that cannot be offset by pricing, or broad profit weakness would show that the low price reflects deteriorating economics rather than a bargain.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: I use only the frozen adjusted-close snapshot through 2026-09-28 and cannot verify later prices, current Treasury yields, inflation or policy data, issuer financial statements, current ETF constituents, duration, credit quality, payout coverage, or valuation multiples. Past returns and 52-week ranges are not fair-value measures. Product and business descriptions rely on general knowledge rather than freshly checked disclosures, and the macro path, catalysts, return, and drawdown estimates are uncertain assumptions.

strategies.riskRationale: For a 24-month, no-rebalancing portfolio, I put 80% in cash or bond ETFs and limit equities to 20%, because an equity drawdown may not recover within the fixed horizon. The 25% cash sleeve earns 0% under the rules but provides a nominal buffer and avoids forced sales; its costs are inflation drag and foregone return. This allocation prioritizes smaller drawdowns over beating SPY in a strong equity rally.

pick.risks: The 70% equity sleeve can fall together in a global risk-off event. VTV, SPY, BRK-B.US and JPM.US overlap in their exposure to U.S. businesses and financial conditions, while EFA and VWO add currency, policy and regional risks rather than dependable hedges. Gold can fall when real rates rise or the dollar strengthens, SHY can lose value if short-term yields rise, and cash has opportunity cost. A recession, credit losses, persistent narrow market leadership or rate shock could produce a decline materially larger than the estimated drawdown.

theses.title: Moderate growth, broader returns
theses.worldView: From the packet date through September 2028, U.S. and major global earnings avoid a sustained multi-quarter contraction, while returns broaden and normalize rather than repeating the recent U.S. market's strong run; this thesis is falsified by a prolonged earnings recession or persistently narrow leadership.
theses.portfolioExpression: VTV is the largest equity sleeve, SPY maintains broad U.S. exposure, and smaller BRK-B.US and JPM.US positions add operating-business and financial-sector exposure. The allocation does not assume these are proven bargains because the snapshot supplies no valuation multiples.

theses.title: Non-U.S. participation
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months, developed ex-U.S. and emerging-market equities deliver competitive aggregate returns, though not necessarily outperforming every year; this thesis is falsified if their earnings and currency outcomes remain materially weaker than those of U.S. equities through the horizon.
theses.portfolioExpression: EFA.US and VWO.US provide geographic and currency diversification and potential relative catch-up. Their weights are modest because both already advanced over the trailing year and sit near their 52-week highs.

theses.title: Insure against macro shocks
theses.worldView: An inflation, real-rate, fiscal or geopolitical risk episode remains plausible enough to affect risk appetite during the next 24 months, though a crisis is not the base case; this thesis is weakened if the period stays orderly and gold fails to diversify equity losses.
theses.portfolioExpression: GLD.US, SHY.US and 12% cash provide partial insurance, not a recession forecast. Cash earns zero and, because this book is fixed, will not be redeployed.

pick.thesis: The base case is modest earnings growth, more normalized market returns and some non-U.S. participation, interrupted by possible macro shocks. VTV is the main value-style exposure; SPY preserves broad U.S. participation, while EFA and VWO diversify regions. Gold, short-term Treasuries and cash temper the risk without removing it; cash is a fixed, zero-return buffer rather than dry powder.

forecasts.reason: A 10% total return is plausible if the global economy avoids a synchronized recession, earnings grow modestly and value or non-U.S. equities participate while the recent 17.6% 12-month SPY gain normalizes rather than repeats. Ordinary equity returns and SHY distributions would need to outweigh the 12% zero-return cash drag; recession or valuation compression could make the realized return negative.

positions.name: Vanguard Value ETF
positions.thesis: VTV is a diversified U.S. value-style equity exposure and is the portfolio's main application of the broader-returns thesis. At the packet close of $218.38, it was up 21.0% over 12 months and about 3.6% below its 52-week high, which does not establish that it is cheap; its role is relative-value exposure if growth broadens, not a claim of a proven discount. Its 25% weight makes it the largest sleeve while spreading company-specific risk.
positions.catalyst: Broader earnings growth and a rotation toward value-style businesses could improve relative returns without requiring a new speculative theme.
positions.invalidation: A recession, margin pressure or sustained narrow leadership by growth stocks could leave VTV underperforming, and it can fall with the wider equity market.

positions.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
positions.thesis: SPY provides broad U.S. equity exposure rather than a value bet in itself. At $765.61, it was up 17.6% over 12 months and only about 1.3% below its 52-week high, so I do not treat it as a bargain; a 15% allocation preserves participation in aggregate U.S. earnings without making the portfolio depend entirely on the value tilt.
positions.catalyst: Continued aggregate earnings growth without a sustained U.S. recession would support broad-market returns.
positions.invalidation: A broad earnings contraction or a sharp decline in the largest index constituents could pull the index down despite its diversification.

positions.name: iShares MSCI EAFE ETF
positions.thesis: EFA provides developed-market equity exposure outside the United States. At $105.04, it was up 18.2% over 12 months and about 3.5% below its 52-week high, so recent performance does not establish a valuation discount; the value here is conditional participation in non-U.S. earnings and diversification if returns broaden globally. The 10% weight limits regional and currency risk.
positions.catalyst: Competitive earnings and currency returns outside the United States could allow developed international markets to contribute meaningfully if U.S. returns normalize.
positions.invalidation: Persistently weaker non-U.S. earnings, unfavorable currency moves or renewed U.S. outperformance could defeat the catch-up thesis.

positions.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
positions.thesis: VWO provides broad emerging-market equity exposure. At $59.69, it was up 13.8% over 12 months and about 2.7% below its 52-week high; that price history is not evidence of a discount, so the value case is conditional on competitive long-run earnings and broader global participation. Its 5% weight reflects higher country, currency and policy risk.
positions.catalyst: Improving earnings and investor participation across emerging markets could help them contribute to global returns over the horizon.
positions.invalidation: Weak earnings, adverse currency or policy shocks, or persistent relative underperformance would disprove the catch-up application.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway Class B
positions.thesis: Berkshire combines operating businesses, insurance and investment activities, applying the thesis through a diversified U.S. company rather than a single narrow growth theme. At $503.09, it was up about 1.6% over 12 months and about 5.0% below its 52-week high, lagging SPY in the snapshot; that relative performance may offer value if the underlying businesses remain resilient, but does not prove undervaluation. A 10% allocation recognizes the diversification within the company as well as its single-company risk.
positions.catalyst: Resilient operating results and continued effective capital allocation could compound value and improve relative performance if growth broadens.
positions.invalidation: A prolonged downturn, deterioration in the businesses or poor capital allocation could prevent the expected compounding and deepen underperformance.

positions.name: JPMorgan Chase
positions.thesis: JPM is a large diversified bank whose prospects depend on credit conditions and economic activity, so it applies the moderate-growth thesis. At $336.59, it was up 9.4% over 12 months and about 7.8% below its 52-week high; the relative pullback is not enough to prove it is cheap without current financial and valuation data. A 5% weight limits the effect of credit, rate and regulatory risks.
positions.catalyst: Steady economic activity, manageable credit losses and continued financial intermediation could support the position.
positions.invalidation: A recession, rising credit losses, unfavorable rate changes or regulatory pressure could undermine the earnings and value case.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: GLD provides gold exposure, which can diversify a conventional equity-and-bond portfolio during some inflation or geopolitical shocks. At $377.91, it was up 9.6% over 12 months but about 23.8% below its 52-week high; that range does not establish intrinsic value because gold produces no business cash flow. The 8% allocation is insurance, not the portfolio's main return engine.
positions.catalyst: Renewed inflation concerns, geopolitical risk or lower real rates could increase demand for gold.
positions.invalidation: Rising real rates, a stronger dollar or subdued demand for safe-haven assets could weigh on gold, which has no cash flow to anchor its value.

positions.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF
positions.thesis: SHY provides short-duration U.S. Treasury exposure as a lower-volatility counterweight to equities, not as a cash equivalent. At $81.11, it was up about 1.5% over 12 months and within roughly 0.9% of its 52-week high; the price history supports its stabilizing role but does not reveal its current yield or guarantee a positive return. Its 10% allocation helps temper portfolio fluctuations.
positions.catalyst: Coupon income and falling short-term yields could support total returns or relative resilience during a risk-off period.
positions.invalidation: A sharp rise in short-term yields or inflation eroding real returns could cause losses, and SHY may not hedge equities in every shock.

I therefore treat value as a conditional, diversified allocation rather than a verified margin-of-safety claim, and the forecast is highly uncertain.

pick.risks: Adobe, Intuit and Oracle together make up 45% of the portfolio and could fall together if AI displaces incumbent software, enterprise spending weakens or long-duration equities are repriced. Constellation Energy is a single-company exposure to power prices, regulation and operating risks. Nike and Home Depot together make up 25% and are exposed to overlapping consumer and housing weakness. Correlations can rise in a selloff; the portfolio is long-only, concentrated and not rebalanced, and losses can be permanent.

theses.title: AI adoption broadens into enterprise workflows.
theses.worldView: From the packet date through September 2028, businesses will expand their use of AI, while established software and data systems retain enough workflow control to monetize some of that use. This is falsified if AI agents replace paid incumbent workflows faster than new paid AI usage develops, or if enterprise technology spending contracts.
theses.portfolioExpression: Allocate 45% to Adobe, Intuit and Oracle rather than extrapolating recent AI infrastructure gains. The value hypothesis is that their sharp price declines overstate permanent loss of embedded workflows, but the supplied prices do not prove that any of these shares is cheap.

theses.title: Reliable electricity remains a strategic bottleneck.
theses.worldView: Over the next 24 months, data-center, electrification and industrial demand will grow faster than additions of dependable generation and grid capacity, supporting the value of existing firm power. This is falsified if load growth disappoints, efficiency or new supply removes the constraint, or electricity prices and regulation fail to support returns.
theses.portfolioExpression: Allocate 20% to Constellation Energy as a concentrated claim on firm-power scarcity. The packet close is below its 52-week high, but that price decline could reflect real deterioration and is not, by itself, evidence of undervaluation.

theses.title: Household demand stabilizes without a boom.
theses.worldView: The United States avoids a prolonged recession through September 2028, and housing-related and discretionary household demand stabilize rather than contract continuously. This is falsified by a prolonged downturn in real household spending, housing activity or consumer demand.
theses.portfolioExpression: Allocate 25% to Nike and Home Depot as cross-sector recovery candidates after sharp price declines. The thesis is conditional on broad household demand stabilizing; it does not assume that either company will recover simply because its share price has fallen.

theses.title: Returns remain dispersed.
theses.worldView: AI competition, financing conditions and energy constraints will produce substantial differences between company outcomes, and broad index strength can coexist with severe losses in individual shares. This is falsified if the next two years bring broad, low-dispersion returns without material company-level drawdowns.
theses.portfolioExpression: Keep 10% in cash because the portfolio is fixed and the packet does not establish valuation or business conditions for the selected laggards. SPY.US is up 17.6% over the trailing 12 months and near its 52-week high, but that is not proof of overvaluation; cash earns 0% and will not be redeployed.

pick.thesis: This is a conditional mean-reversion portfolio built around enterprise AI adoption, firm-power demand and household normalization. The 45% software allocation is the main upside and the main shared risk; Constellation Energy and the two household-related positions provide different, though imperfect, return drivers. I treat price declines as evidence of pessimism, not as proof of cheapness or a measured margin of safety.

forecasts.reason: My single, uncertain expected total-return estimate is +24% over 24 months. It is plausible if the economy avoids a deep recession, AI expands without destroying more incumbent software value than it creates, firm-power demand supports generation economics, and housing and discretionary demand stabilize. The portfolio needs only partial recovery in some laggards, not a return to their prior highs; if those conditions fail, a large loss remains plausible.

positions.name: Adobe
positions.thesis: Under ai-workflow-diffusion, Adobe sells creative and digital-experience software, based on general business knowledge. The packet records an adjusted close of $231.01 on 2026-09-28, a trailing 12-month return of -34.8% and a 52-week range of $193.41 to $360.37. My assumption is that AI will often be embedded in creative workflows rather than fully replace them; product familiarity, file compatibility and repeated professional use are durable mechanisms that could make this price a value opportunity if that assumption holds. The packet does not establish a valuation multiple or current earnings strength. I allocate 18% because a successful monetization response could support a recovery, while direct AI substitution risk argues against a larger weight.
positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be future evidence that AI-assisted products add paid usage, retention or customer spending rather than merely replacing existing paid tools.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if customers broadly move to low-cost AI substitutes, paid usage or spending continues to contract, or AI features do not help Adobe retain valuable workflows.

positions.name: Intuit

positions.name: Oracle

positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be evidence that AI-related and other enterprise workloads translate into durable paid database or cloud usage and returns on infrastructure investment.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if customers migrate away from Oracle's core systems faster than new workloads arrive, or if cloud competition and infrastructure investment prevent new usage from producing attractive returns.

positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be realized growth in large electricity loads that supports durable power demand or attractive long-term supply arrangements.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if data-center or industrial load growth disappoints, efficiency and new supply ease the constraint, regulation limits returns, or operating problems reduce the value of the existing generation.

positions.name: Home Depot

positions.catalyst: A catalyst would be a stabilization in housing transactions and repair spending, potentially supported by less restrictive financing conditions.
positions.invalidation: The thesis fails if weak housing activity and household finances persist, financing remains restrictive for longer than expected, or home-improvement demand deteriorates despite broader economic stabilization.

That concentration offers meaningful upside if the price declines reverse, but leaves the portfolio vulnerable to common-factor losses. I estimate a 45% peak-to-trough drawdown as plausible; a simultaneous recession, AI-displacement shock and repricing of long-duration equities could produce a larger loss, and two years may not be enough to recover. The 10% cash allocation earns 0% and provides only limited loss reduction.
